prompt:
Original Taiwanese game art for "Tainan Gazetteer" (府城夜巡地圖), set in Tainan around 1930.
Style: layered kirie paper cut-outs with fine printed pigment. Thin washi sheets pressed almost
flush; visible, intentional overlaps between cut shapes; very faint short warm contact shadows
under only some edges. Flat matte spot colours with subtle ink-density variation and an
extremely fine low-contrast stencil grain. Palette: warm cream, vermilion, coral, sage, mustard,
indigo, wood brown; slightly muted.
Do NOT use: bevels, foam thickness, 3D extrusion, glow, glossy shading, crumpled or spongy
texture, black outline strokes, gradients, photographic depth of field.
Output: fully TRANSPARENT background, every object complete and separated by clear transparent
gutters, no ground, no base, no cast shadow outside the object, no text, no captions, no logos.
View: front-facing, very slight three-quarter, the same for every object on the sheet.

Use case: stylized-concept, production game sprite sheet. Generate one landscape PNG sprite sheet of exactly six original low streetside connectors, equal 3 columns by 2 rows. Center each complete horizontal segment in its own equal cell with substantial transparent gutters and outer margins. Make the strips broad and low, at game scale one-third to one-half a building's ground-floor height. Left and right ends are straight, flush and aligned for repeating next to themselves, with continuous cap and base elevations where appropriate. For the pots align the feet on the same invisible baseline with a regular cadence for repeat placement. Use directly front-on orthographic elevation for this sheet, overriding the slight three-quarter in the shared style prompt. Zero visible side faces or receding planes, including on masonry and fence caps.

Top left: woodFence, dark brown Japanese dormitory-style fence of vertical wooden boards, with a continuous horizontal wooden rail across the top.
Top middle: ixoraHedge, neatly clipped low long dwarf ixora with dense small dark-green leaves and several round vermilion clusters composed of tiny four-petaled flowers above the foliage.
Top right: brickLowWall, low exposed red brick wall with staggered horizontal brick courses and a straight top course of coping bricks, face-on. A short openwork brick section is optional.
Bottom left: bambooFence, low woven bamboo fence, fine straw and muted ochre strips with simple visible tied cord lashings.
Bottom middle: potRow, exactly four closely spaced terracotta and blue-and-white porcelain pots, containing bougainvillea with magenta bracts, fern fronds and broad lanceolate Chinese evergreen leaves. Treat the row as one asset.
Bottom right: greenHedge, neatly squared-off low dark-green orange jasmine (Murraya paniculata, 月橘/七里香) hedge with sparse small white flowers.

Use the approved machiya, noodleStall, lantern and tileFlower aesthetic: warm muted printed pigment, paper silhouettes, and simplified color separations. Flat cut-paper shapes are the entire visual construction. The top cap on a fence or wall is a single flat horizontal shape. Keep foliage in a small number of overlapping flat ink shapes, avoiding sculpted leaves. Use no directional lighting, modeled volume, rim highlights, relief or halo. Keep each item legible when scaled down. No extras, no cell dividers, no checkerboard or background paint; use real alpha.

Critical production layout: leave the outer 5% of the canvas and the space around each sprite completely empty. Each motif occupies at most 82% of the width of its own cell. Set the motif centers to x=16.7%, 50%, 83.3% and y=25%, 75%. A compact silhouette with sharply cut, mostly opaque washi paper edges. Only final outline antialiasing may be semitransparent. No backdrop tinted pixels, no fog, no soft alpha mattes, no shadows behind the cutout, zero alpha immediately outside each silhouette. Dense opaque paper is cut on the outer contour. Use distinct crisp color fields and extremely fine restrained grain, like a Japanese paper stencil print scanned flat.
